item.title: Reference stays attached to code
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Generated references stay tied to code, registries and RFC evidence.

item.title: AI coding has not had its Rails moment
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Harnesses and models improve every few weeks, and the repositories they work in still explain nothing about themselves. Rails solved that once for people, and nothing equivalent has arrived for agents.

item.title: The repository is half the AI harness
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: AI coding needs more than a capable model. The repository must carry its architecture, relationships, tests and checks in a form the agent can discover and the project can enforce.

item.title: The proof is the expensive part
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Ze uses AI to write code, but an RFC claim only counts after the standard, the tests, the public gap list and the commit process all agree.

item.title: How Ze keeps BGP traffic away from the garbage collector
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: How Ze reuses buffers, borrows wire data and limits copies so repeated routing work creates little garbage.

item.title: One BGP UPDATE, many peers
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: How Ze completes each peer's policy decision before encoding its UPDATE, then reuses an earlier encoding when the complete result matches.

item.title: AI slop is the wrong test
item.dc:creator: Thomas Mangin
item.description: Ze is an AI-written NOS. The useful question is whether the code is constrained, reviewed, tested and measured.
